# Resolution overrides for iac/requirements.txt (uv pip compile --overrides).
# Same idea as the npm `overrides` in package.json: force a transitive
# dependency past a consumer's stale pin to pick up security fixes.
# Path is a per-tool subdir named requirements.txt so SCA scanners recognize it
# by filename (#226) — it is NOT installed directly (it is the --overrides input
# to the iac/requirements.txt compile); the requirements.txt name is purely to
# keep the scanner-requirements tree uniform.
#
# The aiohttp override is GONE (#324): checkov 3.3.8 declared aiohttp<3.14.0,
# but 3.3.13 declares aiohttp<3.15.0, so the patched 3.14.3 now resolves
# NATURALLY and no override is needed for it. Verified against PyPI metadata
# (`requires_dist` of each checkov release) before removal.
#
# asteval: checkov 3.3.13 hard-pins `asteval==1.0.6` (an exact `==`, not a
# range), and 1.0.6 carries two open sandbox-escape advisories —
# GHSA-89v8-rhwq-hf77 (CVE-2026-55244, escape via BaseException subclasses) and
# GHSA-9w56-46f6-3qhx (native memory read/write via numpy ctypes) — both fixed
# in 1.0.9. Because the pin is exact, NO checkov-only recompile can reach a
# patched asteval; the override is the only channel. checkov imports asteval in
# exactly one place, `checkov/terraform/graph_builder/variable_rendering/
# safe_eval_functions.py` (Terraform variable rendering), which our CI
# invocation (`checkov -d cdk.out --framework cloudformation`) never loads; the
# CI checkov gate is verified to pass unchanged on 1.0.9.
# Because this override violates checkov's declared metadata, the install in
# security.yml uses --no-deps (the lockfile is a complete, hash-verified
# closure, so dependency resolution at install time is redundant).
# Drop this override once checkov's asteval pin allows >=1.0.9.
asteval==1.0.9
